entry.title: 3Speak: Lightning Strikes, Podcasts Play, Thumbnails Shine

link.title: 3Speak: Lightning Strikes, Podcasts Play, Thumbnails Shine

entry.content:
![3Speak dev update, October 28 to November 4, 2026](https://images.hive.blog/DQmXwcohU9s42mDcdy6LmmNeUxsb3unP8YtSqMWvAtXHVJz/thumbnail.png) **The short version** - **Tip with Lightning:** any Lightning wallet can tip a creator, no Hive account needed, and creators can get tips in their own wallet. - **Import your videos** from YouTube or TikTok, with title, description, tags and thumbnail filled in for you. - A **thumbnail editor** in the uploader: text, stickers and any frame of your video. - **The Hive galaxy:** a 3D map of a channel's follows, to discover new creators. - **Stories** are open to every Hive account. - **3Speak is a podcast app now:** follow any podcast in the world, with charts, chapters, transcripts, offline listening and a full podcast player, plus sponsor spots and a pop-out player for 3Speak audio. - Under the hood: a rebuilt encoder for community operators, smarter retries for uploads, Butter Drive for big files and a new Snapie release. --- ## 🌐 3speak.tv website [new-3speak-tv](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/new-3speak-tv) · 10 releases, all live
### Tip with Lightning Every tip window now has a **Lightning** tab. Anyone with a Lightning wallet can tip a creator, no Hive account needed: the tip goes through the creator's v4v.app address, and a paid invoice is picked up by itself. ![The Lightning tab in the 3Speak tip window](https://images.hive.blog/DQmRN2AuiK2X3FAakMQH92bF8xLRo1a6z1xr8fmRjVH4PEy/tip.png) - Creators can also receive Lightning tips **in their own wallet** (Settings, Connections tab). - You can tip **without signing in**, and set up **monthly tips**. - Lightning tips show under [Supporters](https://3speak.tv/@badadib?tab=supporters), in sats. - Tip buttons on [Shorts](https://3speak.tv/shorts), in the audio player, and now also in the 3Speak video player and the audio embed on other sites. ([#536](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/new-3speak-tv/pull/536), [#540](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/new-3speak-tv/pull/540))
### Import your videos Bring your videos over from YouTube or TikTok. First, prove the channel is yours: 1. Open **Settings** (the gear at the top), go to **Connections** and then **Linked profiles**. 2. Pick the platform and copy your personal 3Speak code into your channel's public description. 3. Enter your channel and press **Verify**. Once it is linked, you can remove the code from your description again. ![Link your channel in Settings, then import](https://images.hive.blog/DQmUqNG3R6AqV63eFTaR5xQKL3fBnyWiQvoaD6LTHUWVVAm/link.png) Then use **Import videos** on your profile or in the upload window, or open [Import videos](https://3speak.tv/youtube-import). Title, description, tags and thumbnail are filled in for you, and you can import a whole batch at once. ([#536](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/new-3speak-tv/pull/536), [#537](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/new-3speak-tv/pull/537), [#544](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/new-3speak-tv/pull/544))
### A thumbnail editor in the uploader Step 2 of the [upload](https://3speak.tv/upload) now has a thumbnail editor. Pick any moment of your video, zoom and drag the frame, add text in 26 fonts with an outline or a box behind it, and place stickers, including 3Speak and Hive branding or your own images. **Download** saves exactly the picture that gets uploaded. On phones and tablets our server cuts the frame for you, so it works there too. ([#544](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/new-3speak-tv/pull/544))
### The Hive galaxy
![The Hive galaxy on 3Speak](https://images.hive.blog/DQmVwb5jAZUwaHPTg6zSk6vnxoAP8pbkBmGdF59gmfsXWSA/galaxy.png)
On desktop, the planet button on a profile opens the **Hive galaxy**: a 3D map of who a channel follows and the creators those follows lead to. Look at a channel's Following, its Followers or the friends who follow each other, and choose how deep to scan, from an Orbit of 120 accounts up to Deep space with 5,000. Accounts that the same people follow form **circles**, so you can see the little communities around a channel at a glance. Next to the map, **Creators to discover** lists the accounts many of the scanned people follow, and filters keep it to active accounts, a minimum reputation or creators with videos on 3Speak. Drag to turn the map, scroll to zoom, click a star to focus it and click the centre to fly back. Try [badadib's galaxy](https://3speak.tv/galaxy/badadib). ([#539](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/new-3speak-tv/pull/539), [3speakchecks #101](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speakchecks/pull/101))
### Stories for every Hive account Any logged-in Hive account can now post a 24-hour [Story](https://3speak.tv/shorts), from the Upload menu or from your own avatar in the stories row. Hovering an avatar in the row turns it around to a creator card: when they last posted, their bio and their follower, video, short and audio counts. ([#535](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/new-3speak-tv/pull/535), [#542](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/new-3speak-tv/pull/542))
### Podcasts and the new Audio page The biggest change of the week: the [Audio page](https://3speak.tv/audio) is now a full podcast app, for 3Speak audio and for any podcast out there. ![Add any podcast to 3Speak](https://images.hive.blog/DQmbHi7CUb2z6cpzNnz8YuQCrSD1tueoAx8EZHLY2cUExFG/add-podcast.png) - **Any podcast, not just Hive:** follow a show under External by searching for it, pasting its RSS feed, an Apple Podcasts or Overcast link or the show's website, or importing an OPML file from another app. - **Find new shows:** top charts for your country and category, trending podcasts by language, and a People search that finds the shows a host or guest appears in. - **Show and episode pages** with seasons, trailers, chapters marked on the timeline, transcripts that follow along, and the hosts and guests. - **Mine, Discover and Trends** split the Audio page into three views, and phones get a Player tab of their own. ![The 3Speak audio player, button by button](https://images.hive.blog/DQmZgfnuBDaMFFGUPp6x3qRsYXmVwyryzRwzigJsAkEBCPa/player-buttons.png) - **A real podcast player:** speed from 0.5x to 2x, 15-second skips, a sleep timer, Voice boost and Skip silence, casting to a speaker or TV, and your phone's lock screen controls. - **Share a moment:** a link that starts at the current time, or a clip of 15 to 90 seconds. - **Listen offline:** save episodes and 3Speak audio, and without a connection the Audio page opens your downloads. - **Never miss an episode:** new-episode alerts in the bell and as push notifications, and shows can add new episodes to your queue by themselves. - **Tip podcasters** in sats, straight from the podcast's own payment details. - **Every 3Speak audio has its own page**, and an all-audio playlist can be followed like a podcast. The full tour, with a screenshot for every button, is in [our podcast post](https://peakd.com/@mantequilla-soft/3speak-the-whole-podcast-universe-now-on-hive-2026-10-31). ([#536](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/new-3speak-tv/pull/536), [#539](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/new-3speak-tv/pull/539))
### Added since the podcast post ![Audio spots on the 3Speak advertise page](https://images.hive.blog/DQmNh8EsKt6eLaK4C2SdcwEZUxAjTgMdpCLfqJmn3pvWZtM/audio-ads.png) - **Sponsor spots in audio:** advertisers can book spoken tickers or their own audio clip on the [advertise page](https://3speak.tv/advertise). Creators choose in Settings whether ads play on their audio. - **A pop-out player** on desktop that fits whatever window you give it. - **A smarter queue:** tapping a cover while something plays adds it to the queue, and playlists offer **Add all** or **Add new**. - **Comment, Hype and reblog** any 3Speak audio right from the player. - **Continue listening** on [Mine](https://3speak.tv/audio?view=mine), and what you listened to shows in your Watched history, in a new Audio tab. - **New audio in [Discover](https://3speak.tv/discover):** the last 3 days of audio, one per creator. - **Earn while you listen:** agree once in Settings and your listening counts toward listener rewards, which start once we have checked the numbers. - 3Speak shows you follow under External get votes, comments, Hype and tips, and warm-up musicians and podcasters can now upload audio too. ([#538](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/new-3speak-tv/pull/538), [#539](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/new-3speak-tv/pull/539), [#540](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/new-3speak-tv/pull/540), [#541](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/new-3speak-tv/pull/541), [#543](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/new-3speak-tv/pull/543), [#544](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/new-3speak-tv/pull/544))
### Small touches ![Emoji in comments and menus that open on hover](https://images.hive.blog/DQmTvPf5DreWJrTYXjwRuedRRfDu6LDi87iwXyRqsSMPb7t/touches.png) - Type `:` in any comment box for an emoji list, and `:fire:` turns into 🔥. - The bell, Share, chat, settings and profile menus open when you rest the mouse on them. - Video previews on cards fade in and out smoothly. - Sharing a vertical video from your phone to 3Speak opens the Shorts uploader. - Profiles keep their Hive badges when a Hive server is busy: the site switches servers by itself. - "Mark all read" now clears the newest notification too. - The tip nudge no longer stops autoplay and channel surfing. ([#539](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/new-3speak-tv/pull/539), [#542](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/new-3speak-tv/pull/542), [#544](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/new-3speak-tv/pull/544)) --- ## ⚡ Feeds and API [3speakchecks](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speakchecks) · 22 changes The "checker" is the service behind 3Speak's feeds, ads, tips and the Audio page. ![Snapie shorts, galaxy scan and stories row in numbers](https://images.hive.blog/DQmbs91jeqpCY8iCwBnLop5t5w7xLgY2exYFxMU4srB2KFD/checker.png) - **Snapie shorts are back on 3Speak.** Shorts uploaded through Snapie stopped reaching 3Speak's lists on October 5. They do again, and the 143 stuck shorts were restored. ([#96](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speakchecks/pull/96)) - **Lightning tips** are recorded and shown under Supporters. ([#91](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speakchecks/pull/91)) - **The galaxy** reads follows from HafSQL, so a scan of up to 5,000 accounts takes 1 to 3.5 seconds. ([#101](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speakchecks/pull/101)) - **Listening time** for all audio, measured like watch time: only forward playback counts, and it stays anonymous. ([#99](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speakchecks/pull/99)) - **The stories row** keeps a creator for 3 days after their latest short instead of 7, so it changes more often. ([#111](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speakchecks/pull/111)) - **[Video Pulse](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/videopulse)** gets a list of older videos people are watching again, so they can go back on fast storage. Video Pulse itself runs as a dry run for now. ([#104](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speakchecks/pull/104)) - The server side of podcasts, audio ads, warm-up audio and the Audio page. ([#92](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speakchecks/pull/92), [#95](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speakchecks/pull/95), [#97](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speakchecks/pull/97), [#98](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speakchecks/pull/98), [#102](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speakchecks/pull/102), [#103](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speakchecks/pull/103), [#105](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speakchecks/pull/105), [#106](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speakchecks/pull/106), [#107](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speakchecks/pull/107), [#108](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speakchecks/pull/108), [#109](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speakchecks/pull/109), [#110](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speakchecks/pull/110), [#112](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speakchecks/pull/112), [#113](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speakchecks/pull/113), [#114](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speakchecks/pull/114), [#115](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speakchecks/pull/115)) --- ## 🎞️ Encoder [3speakencoder](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speakencoder) · 21 changes Community members run encoders that turn uploads into streamable video. This week the encoder got a full overhaul for them: ![Encoder and upload changes, before and after](https://images.hive.blog/DQmW5ae9EzA5jTpNPzW54XVMvekGafJkTE7rrpDW2iAwG5r/encoder.png) - **Works with FFmpeg 8 and newer** again: before, it failed to start. ([#54](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speakencoder/pull/54)) - **Installers that work:** Windows finds and checks FFmpeg without admin rights, Linux and macOS get Node 20+ and a current IPFS (Kubo 0.43.1), Apple Silicon and Fedora are covered, and the encoder can start on boot. ([#51](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speakencoder/pull/51), [#72](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speakencoder/pull/72), [#73](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speakencoder/pull/73), [#74](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speakencoder/pull/74)) - **A new dashboard** in a Tokyo Night look, installable as an app, with an optional password. ([#53](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speakencoder/pull/53), [#57](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speakencoder/pull/57), [#60](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speakencoder/pull/60), [#68](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speakencoder/pull/68)) - **Updates:** the encoder knows which version it runs, tells you when it is behind, checks on demand and can update itself if you switch that on. ([#56](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speakencoder/pull/56), [#58](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speakencoder/pull/58), [#66](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speakencoder/pull/66), [#75](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speakencoder/pull/75)) - **Uploads go only to hot nodes.** If that fails, a local copy is kept, tracked and moved back later. ([#62](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speakencoder/pull/62), [#63](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speakencoder/pull/63)) - Tests and checks on every change, and up-to-date docs. ([#50](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speakencoder/pull/50), [#52](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speakencoder/pull/52), [#55](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speakencoder/pull/55), [#59](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speakencoder/pull/59), [#61](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speakencoder/pull/61), [#64](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speakencoder/pull/64)) --- ## 📤 Upload service [embedvideos](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/embedvideos) · 5 changes - A failed encoding job is **retried on a different encoder**. ([#43](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/embedvideos/pull/43), [#44](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/embedvideos/pull/44)) - An upload can no longer get stuck at "uploading" when the IPFS announce hangs. ([#36](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/embedvideos/pull/36)) - The old supernode is out of the upload path. ([#38](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/embedvideos/pull/38)) - The admin view shows which version every community encoder runs. ([#41](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/embedvideos/pull/41)) --- ## ▶️ Video player [snapievideoplayer](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/snapievideoplayer) · 1 change The player now has a **Tip** button. It opens the 3speak.tv tip window with HIVE / HBD and Lightning, so viewers can tip even when they watch a 3Speak video embedded on another site. ([#55](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/snapievideoplayer/pull/55)) --- ## 🎧 Audio embed [snapieaudio](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/snapieaudio) · 3 changes The audio player other sites embed got a **Tip** button too, plays 3Speak's sponsor spots, and reports listening time anonymously, the same way the player on 3speak.tv does. ([#8](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/snapieaudio/pull/8), [#9](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/snapieaudio/pull/9), [#10](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/snapieaudio/pull/10)) --- ## 📱 Snapie [snapie-io](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/snapie-io) · 3 releases - Pages that don't exist answer with a real "not found". - The home feed no longer hangs on "Loading..." when a Hive node is slow. - A post that fails to load has a **Retry** button, and Escape closes a conversation. - Profile and post details are cached, so slow Hive nodes hurt less. - Fixes for chat, unread notifications and payouts that flashed $0.000. ([#316](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/snapie-io/pull/316), [#320](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/snapie-io/pull/320), [#326](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/snapie-io/pull/326)) --- ## ☁️ Butter Drive [butterdrive](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/butterdrive) · 2 changes Butter Drive, the desktop app for Butter Cloud storage, now uploads files over 100 MB in parts, and [version 0.1.1](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/butterdrive/releases) is out with installers for macOS, Windows and Linux. ([#2](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/butterdrive/pull/2), [#3](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/butterdrive/pull/3)) --- That's it for this week. Most of our code is open on GitHub at [github.com/Mantequilla-Soft](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft). Questions, bug reports or ideas? Drop them in the comments below.
[![Mantequilla Soft](https://images.hive.blog/DQmSCTXSSRQ4R5Xq2pGTTiiMuSsTcJYAy1ozfkb35M7jVzB/mantequilla-soft-logo.png)](https://www.mantequilla-soft.com) **[GitHub](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft) · [Website](https://www.mantequilla-soft.com) · [Snapie](https://snapie.io) · [3Speak](https://3speak.tv)**

entry.title: Magi 0.12: BTC Vault v2, POA seats.

link.title: Magi 0.12: BTC Vault v2, POA seats.

entry.content:
![image.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmbuDK3H8pZo3Zv4VtoCrPYipYxs3viM4nppVviyL6vPPZ/image.png) The biggest Magi upgrade so far is rolling out. Mainnet moves from consensus 0.3 straight to 0.12 in one step, covering Bitcoin custody, how the witness committee is formed, how HIVE is staked behind nodes, and how the network's threshold keys are kept healthy. ## Why this release - **Bitcoin custody stays with the current committee.** After every election the vault key's shares are reshared to the new committee. Vault v2 adds full key rotation: a brand-new key is generated by the current committee and proven, then the coins move to it on-chain automatically, so key shares from former members end up guarding an empty vault. - **POA.** Witnesses now hold ratified seats, admitted by a vote of the existing seats, with equal weight per seat and collateral that stays bonded after a witness leaves for 3 days. - **Steadier threshold signing.** Key resharing and signing keep going when a node is slow or unreachable: an unresponsive node is left out of the next attempt instead of stalling the rest. ## At a glance | | Node (go-vsc-node) | BTC contract (utxo-mapping) | |---|---|---| | Range | main (consensus 0.3) -> develop b10d0fab | vault v2 (#29) -> main 23ff9b8 | | Commits | 361 | 21 | | Code | +22,787 / -2,422 lines, 181 files | +7,036 / -386 lines, 19 files | | Tests | +56,143 / -982 lines, 372 files | +10,317 / -64 lines, 64 files | | Files changed | 563 | 88 | Together that is about **29,800 lines of code** and **66,500 lines of tests** added, more than two lines of tests for every line of code. | Consensus version | Theme | |---|---| | 0.4 | Election safety and ledger fixes | | 0.7 | Proof-of-Authority seats, TSS session and key lifecycle rules, BTC signing safety halts | | 0.8 | BTC Vault v2, BLS and commitment hardening | | 0.9 | POA and TSS refinements, gateway weights, reward scoring | | 0.10 | Proof verification pricing, block apply hardening | | 0.11 | Vault key custody | | 0.12 | New vault keys reshared into the committee before activation, peer identity proofs, deposit memo improvements | ## BTC Vault v2 The vault can now move to a brand-new key. The contract owner starts a rotation, the current committee generates the new key, and the previous vault keeps serving until the new one is ready. A new key goes live only after it has produced a verified signature, and coins move to it only after it has been reshared into the committee, so every new vault is shown to work before it holds funds. The mapping bot then sweeps the coins from the old vault to the new one in batches that run in parallel, older coins included. Miner fees for the migration come from a dedicated fee reserve, so user balances are not touched, and small coins are swept at a fee that fits their size. A withdrawal that cannot be built right away, for example mid-rotation, is queued in order and paid once the vault can build it. Deposits to a previous vault address keep being credited for about 30 days after that vault is emptied, and an old vault is retired only once it is empty. A retiring vault key can only sign transfers to its successor vault. If anyone proves that a vault coin moved outside the contract's own spends, vault signing pauses, and governance can pause it as well. | Feature | What it does | |---|---| | Key rotation | The contract owner starts a rotation and the current committee generates a new vault key. The previous vault keeps serving until the new one is ready. | | Proven before activation | A new key goes live only after it has produced a verified signature and been reshared into the committee, so every new vault is shown to work before any funds move to it. | | Automatic migration | The mapping bot sweeps coins from the old vault to the new one in parallel batches, older coins included. | | Fee reserve | Migration miner fees come from a dedicated fee reserve. User balances are never touched. | | Adaptive sweep fees | Small coins are swept at a fee that fits their size instead of holding up the migration. | | Withdrawal queue | A withdrawal that cannot be built right away, for example mid-rotation, is queued in order and paid automatically. | | Deposit grace period | Deposits to a previous vault address keep being credited for about 30 days after that vault is emptied. | | Retirement only when empty | An old vault is retired only once it is empty. | | Scoped signing | A retiring vault key can only sign transfers to its successor vault. | | Safety halt | Vault signing pauses if a vault coin is shown to have moved outside the contract's own spends, and governance can pause it as well. | ## Proof-of-Authority witness seats This is about who gets to run the network and hold a share of the vault key. Until now, the committee was formed mostly by stake weight: put up enough HIVE and you could be voted in. For a system guarding real Bitcoin, that is risky — a well-funded newcomer could buy their way onto the committee quickly. Proof-of-Authority replaces that with "seats." A seat is an approved spot on the committee, and you only get one if the witnesses who already hold seats vote you in (two thirds have to agree). Every seat counts equally in elections, no matter how much HIVE is behind it, so no one can dominate by sheer size. Just as important, leaving is not instant: your collateral stays bonded for a few days after you step down, and stays locked entirely while any vault you helped guard still holds funds. That means a witness cannot grab a key share and immediately walk away — their money is on the line until the coins they were trusted with are safe. Proof of authority is a transitional step and will be loosened over time. | Feature | What it does | |---|---| | Seats | Only witnesses holding a ratified seat can be elected to the committee. | | Admission vote | New seats are admitted by two thirds of existing seats (`vsc.admit_vote`). | | Equal weight | Every seat carries the same election weight. | | Churn cap | Limits how many new members can join in a single election. | | Exit halt | A departing witness's collateral stays bonded for 3 days after it leaves the committee. | | Bond backs custody | A witness's bond stays locked while a vault it holds a key share of still holds funds, and is released once that vault has been emptied. | | Smooth transition | Founding seats are seeded from the current committee, and each founding member proves its consensus and gateway keys. | ## TSS and consensus hardening TSS (threshold signature scheme) is the technology behind the shared vault key. The key is split into pieces held by the committee members, and a signature needs enough of them to cooperate, so no single member, and no small group, can sign alone. Consensus is the separate process by which nodes agree on the state of the chain. Both are plumbing most users never see, but they matter in different ways. If consensus stalls, everything on Magi waits. If TSS stalls, BTC withdrawals wait for their signature, while deposits keep being credited, because crediting a deposit needs consensus, not a signature. This release is a batch of reliability and safety fixes for that plumbing. The headline: a key reshare no longer stalls when one or two nodes fail to take part. A reshare needs every listed member to answer, so a single silent node fails the attempt for everyone. Now, when at least two thirds of the committee confirm that a node did not take part, the next attempt goes ahead without it, up to two nodes per attempt, and never so many that the committee drops below its minimum. The rest are guardrails against dangerous edge cases. A reshare can never produce a key that less than a majority of the committee can sign. An election can never shrink the committee below its safe minimum. Holders of the live vault key stay available to sign after they leave the election, so the key keeps its signers while the committee changes. A node banned for repeated failures is let back in when a session would otherwise be short of members, so a ban alone never leaves a key unable to sign. Several ways to game the committee are closed off. | Feature | What it does | |---|---| | Unresponsive nodes skipped | If one or two nodes fail a key reshare, the committee leaves them out of the retry so the reshare completes. A key is never reshared below its signing threshold. | | Signing threshold kept | A reshare never leaves a key that less than a majority of the committee can sign. | | Quorum first | Bans yield when a session would otherwise lack the members it needs. | | Committee floor | An election can never produce a committee below the minimum size. | | Key holders stay available | Holders of the active vault key can still sign after leaving the election. | | Peer identity proofs | A witness announcing a P2P identity must prove it owns that key. | | BLS weight dedup | Duplicate keys in a committee count once. | | Commitment size cap | Oversized TSS commitment bundles are rejected up front. | | Safer version upgrades | A forced consensus version floor still needs the outgoing committee's quorum. | | Duplicate-safe block apply | A transaction already handled by an earlier block is never applied twice. | | Proof verification pricing | SP1 Groth16 verification is charged by the work it does, ready for proof-based bridges. | ## Gateway, ledger and API These are the parts users actually touch. The gateway is how value moves in and out — deposits and withdrawals between Hive and Magi. The ledger is the running record of everyone's balances. The API is the set of queries that wallets, dashboards and apps read from. The fixes here are smaller and more concrete than the deep protocol work above: unstaking HBD from savings now releases the stake the way you would expect, deposit memos accept a `to=hive:` tag for any valid Hive account, and when a transaction fails it now keeps a readable reason that apps can show you instead of a silent error. Nothing here changes how the network is secured — it just makes the everyday experience smoother and clearer. | Feature | What it does | |---|---| | HBD savings unstake | Unstaking HBD from savings releases the stake as expected. | | Deposit memos | `to=hive:` memos are accepted for every valid Hive account name. | | Gateway weights | Gateway multisig keys get equal weight under POA. | | Clearer errors | A failed transaction keeps its reason, visible through the API. | | Reward scoring | Pendulum rewards score only fully closed block slots. | ## How it was tested - About 66,500 lines of new tests, including full-network devnet scenarios covering rotation, seats, staking and fault conditions. - Repeated live BTC vault rotations on testnet. After 12 of them, a full funds audit found every vault coin on chain and matching the books, and HIVE and HBD gateway balances reconciled against Hive L1. - The first mainnet migration was rehearsed in tests shaped on the live mainnet vault. - Delegations, races between concurrent transactions, deposit memos, withdrawals and invalid inputs were all exercised live on testnet. ## Rollout 1. Node operators update to the new build. Nodes on watchtower update automatically; manual operators pull the new image and restart (stop, wait a minute, start). 2. Once the committee runs the new build, consensus 0.12 is proposed and activates on-chain. 3. The BTC contract is upgraded. Contract updates take effect 48 hours after submission, a built-in safety window. 4. The first vault rotation moves the BTC to a new key generated by the current committee. ## Next: EVM Ethereum is next. The EVM bridge is built on the same committee-secured model, and its mapping bot is already part of this build, waiting for launch. Proof verification pricing in 0.10 is part of that groundwork. More soon. Thanks to every witness operator and tester who ran the testnet builds. This release is the foundation for bringing more chains to Magi. --- *Posted via Lumen*</div>
Source: Magi 0.12: BTC Vault v2, POA seats. by @magi.network
</div>

link.title: 3Speak Encoder: big update for node operators 🎬

entry.content:
Greetings and Salutations Hiveans! 👋 Over the last few days we've shipped the biggest batch of changes the 3Speak encoder has had in a while: **20 updates** covering installation, the dashboard, uploads and reliability. If you run an encoder for the community, this post is for you. There's a short **"How to upgrade"** section at the end. ![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mantequilla-soft/23wWwQmgLtrubjegAvbwjFrqsT9xTAqgeUaL5ign8R6bfNrJ4RAky1xtQwpZ56VDPYtSj.jpg) --- ## 🚀 Installing is now one line New operators can get going with a single command: **Linux / Mac** ``` curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speakencoder/main/install.sh | bash ``` **Windows (PowerShell)** ``` iwr -useb https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speakencoder/main/install.ps1 | iex ``` The installer works out what's missing and installs it: Git, Node.js, FFmpeg and IPFS. Then it downloads the encoder, sets it up from a few questions and checks that everything works before it finishes. Every change is tested by installing on fresh Windows, Mac and Linux machines (Ubuntu, Debian, Fedora and Arch). What got fixed along the way: - **Windows: "FFmpeg not found" is gone.** The old installer needed an administrator window. Without one it failed quietly and still said everything was fine. It now uses winget, which comes with Windows 10 and 11 and needs no admin rights. It checks that FFmpeg actually runs and saves its location, so the encoder always finds it. - **Mac:** works out of the box on Apple Silicon Macs. - **Linux:** Fedora and Arch are supported, and older systems like Ubuntu 22.04 get a recent Node.js automatically. - **Start automatically (optional):** the installer can make IPFS and the encoder start whenever the computer boots (Linux) or you log in (Mac, Windows). No more forgetting to restart your node after a reboot. - **New `npm run doctor` command:** checks Node.js, FFmpeg and IPFS and tells you in plain words what's missing. If something's off, run this first. ⚠️ **Important for people who installed a while ago:** an old installer option ("Gateway mode") set up encoders that **never received any jobs**. If your encoder has sat idle for a long time, that may be why. The encoder now warns at startup with `No job source enabled`. The fix is three lines in your `.env`: ``` EMBED_SYSTEM_ENABLED=true EMBED_SYSTEM_MODE=community EMBED_GATEWAY_URL=https://embed.3speak.tv ``` --- ## 🖥️ A brand new dashboard ![Screenshot 2026-10-31 at 1.35.27 PM.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mantequilla-soft/23swe5kv3u8AuRLjDoSN95hkNEZ57cbkw4gzbx2qeWRdCVPVrRUg8UofrzdwjZCMgyR7A.png) The local dashboard at `http://localhost:3001` got a full redesign, inspired by the tiling-desktop look of Tokyo Night colours theme. - **Easier to read at a glance:** the current job, encoder health, recent jobs, anything that needs your attention, and the live log. - **Accurate status:** the dashboard used to show "Offline" while the encoder was busy and perfectly fine. It now tells apart *Encoding*, *Not responding* (frozen), *Unreachable* (stopped, or the port is blocked) and *Offline* (shutting down). - **Health numbers:** how responsive the encoder process is, and how long it's been up. - **Install it as an app:** on your phone or computer, the dashboard can be installed like an app with its own icon. Use **Install app** in the top bar in Chrome, Edge or Android, or **Add to Home Screen** in Safari. This needs the dashboard on HTTPS, so it's for operators who reach their node through a domain name. - **Optional password and safer defaults:** you can now set a dashboard password, or limit the dashboard to your own machine. It also blocks a class of attacks where another website open in your browser tries to control your encoder. --- ## 🔄 Updates and versions - **Know when you're behind:** the dashboard shows which version you run and how many updates you're missing, with a link to what changed. **Check for updates** checks right away. - **One-click updates (optional):** turn it on with `SELF_UPDATE_ENABLED=true` and an `UPDATE_PASSWORD`, and you can update from the dashboard. The encoder finishes its current jobs first, updates, and restarts itself. If anything goes wrong, it rolls back to the version that was working. It's off by default, works on git installs (not Docker), and needs the encoder started with the included start script, which the installer's shortcuts use. - **No more half-updated nodes:** if the encoder can't build after an update (most often because files belong to another user after a `sudo` command), it now stops with a clear message instead of starting on a mix of old and new code. - **Your version, visible to 3Speak:** encoders now report which version they run and how far behind they are, so we can see at a glance who needs to update and reach out. It's only the version: no personal data, and nothing changes about the jobs you get. --- ## 📦 Uploads: simpler and more honest - **Uploads go to 3Speak's hotnodes only.** The old upload path to the "supernode" has been removed for good. - **When an upload fails:** by default the job is reported as failed, so 3Speak knows and can give it to another encoder. Before, the encoder fell back to the old supernode. - **Optional local backup (`ENABLE_LOCAL_FALLBACK=true`):** if the upload fails, your node keeps the video on its own IPFS node and keeps trying to move it to a hotnode in the background. The video keeps the same address, so viewers never notice. Only recommended for operators with fast and reliable internet connections. - **See where every backed-up video stands:** the dashboard's storage section lists each one as *waiting to move*, *moved*, *removed* or *deleted*, with dates and the video's owner and link. One click checks the video is reachable before you do anything by hand. --- ## 🛠️ Under the hood - **FFmpeg 8 support:** the encoder failed to start on FFmpeg 8 and newer (`Input format lavfi is not available`). Fixed. - **Docker:** the production Docker image and compose file wouldn't build or run. Both are fixed; the compose file runs the encoder together with its own IPFS node. - **Steadier startup:** the encoder waits up to 90 seconds for IPFS instead of giving up at once, which matters when both start together at boot. - **Automatic tests:** every change now runs through automatic tests on Linux and Windows, plus the full install on Windows, Mac and several Linux distributions. - **Documentation:** the README and install guides have been rewritten to match how things work today. --- ## ✅ How to upgrade **Requirement:** Node.js **20 or newer**. Check with `node -v`. If you have 18 or older, update Node.js first from https://nodejs.org (the LTS version), or let the installer do it. **Option A: you installed with git (most operators)** In your encoder folder (usually `~/3speak-encoder`, or `C:\Users\\3speak-encoder` on Windows): ``` git pull npm ci npm run doctor ``` Then restart the encoder the way you normally start it. Your settings and your encoder identity stay as they are. **Option B: run the installer again** Run the one-line command from the top of this post. It keeps your encoder identity and saves your old settings as `.env.bak`. If you had changed extra settings (a dashboard password, local backup, and so on), copy them back from `.env.bak` into `.env`. **Option C: Docker** ``` git pull GIT_COMMIT=$(git rev-parse HEAD) docker compose -f docker-compose.production.yml up -d --build ``` **Good to know after upgrading:** - **Opening the dashboard by a name** (like `encoder.mydomain.com` instead of an IP address)? Add that name to `.env` as `DASHBOARD_ALLOWED_HOSTS=encoder.mydomain.com` and restart. Otherwise the dashboard answers "Host not allowed". This is part of the new protection against malicious websites. - **Don't use `sudo`** for `git pull`, `npm` or starting the encoder. It leaves files the encoder can't update later. If you did in the past, fix it once on Linux or Mac with `sudo chown -R $(whoami): .` in the encoder folder. - **Something not working?** Run `npm run doctor` first. It points at the problem in plain words. --- Thanks to everyone running an encoder: you're the ones keeping 3Speak videos flowing. 🙌 If you hit a problem, open an issue on [GitHub](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speakencoder/issues) or find us on Discord.
[![Mantequilla Soft](https://images.hive.blog/DQmSCTXSSRQ4R5Xq2pGTTiiMuSsTcJYAy1ozfkb35M7jVzB/mantequilla-soft-logo.png)](https://www.mantequilla-soft.com) **[GitHub](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft) · [Website](https://www.mantequilla-soft.com) · [Snapie](https://snapie.io) · [3Speak](https://3speak.tv)**
</div> *— The Mantequilla Soft team*</div>
Source: 3Speak Encoder: big update for node operators 🎬 by @mantequilla-soft
</div>

entry.title: Exchange node in four lines (Hive 1.28.8)
entry.content:
How many commands does it take to run a Hive node for an exchange? Four. One of them is `cd`, and the last one is for watching the logs while you drink your coffee ;-) Remember [Hive Node Setup for the Smart, the Dumb, and the Lazy](/@gtg/hive-node-setup-for-the-smart-the-dumb-and-the-lazy)? This one is for the lazy. ## No scripts, one compose file We were asked for a "cloud-native" way to run a node: no helper scripts, just one declarative file. Hive 1.28.8 has exactly that: [`docker/exchange`](https://github.com/openhive-network/hive/tree/1.28.8/docker/exchange), a Docker Compose setup for an exchange node. I serve a copy of it at https://gtg.openhive.network/get/exchange/ - slightly modified from upstream: it tracks the accounts I chose to support, so it matches my exchange snapshot, and it keeps the block log and the snapshot in plain folders next to the compose file.
![Cyberpunk-Hive-chan.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmTZJyTj2iXDnJBRZ8ZpEN4FeGZMwm65H1hvGKvrSU1Muv/Cyberpunk-Hive-chan.png)Cyberpunk Hive chan, generated by AI during HiveFest 2026
## What's in the box ``` hive-exchange-1.28.8 ├── .env <- your settings: ports, BLOCK_LOG_DIR, SNAPSHOT_URL ├── compose.yml <- the node itself, nothing to edit ├── config.ini <- hived options and the tracked accounts ├── README.md ├── blockchain <- your block_log, or block_log_part.* files └── snapshot <- the unpacked snapshot (downloaded here if empty) ``` **You have a block log?** If you had a Hive node running recently, you probably do. It's preferred and recommended to re-use it. Blocks never change. That's the whole point. Put it into `blockchain`: one big `block_log` file or a set of `block_log_part.*` files, both work. Or keep it where it is and point `BLOCK_LOG_DIR` in `.env` to it. **No block log?** Leave `blockchain` empty. The node then runs pruned (see below). The snapshot takes care of itself: if `snapshot` is empty, the node downloads my exchange snapshot (6.3 GB) into it. Already have it unpacked? Put it there. ## The four lines ``` wget -qO- https://gtg.openhive.network/get/exchange/hive-exchange-1.28.8.tgz | tar xz cd hive-exchange-1.28.8 docker compose up -d docker compose logs -f hived ``` Unpack it on the disk where the block log is (or will be). If your block log stays where it is, add one line before `docker compose up -d`: ``` echo BLOCK_LOG_DIR=/path/to/your/blockchain >> .env ``` ~~Four lines~~ Five lines. The coffee is still the last one. The node loads the snapshot, replays your block log from the snapshot's block on, and syncs the rest from the network. Without a block log, it does the same minus the replay. Minutes, not even hours. When the log says `entering live mode`, press Ctrl+C. That stops the log, not the node. `docker compose ps` shows the node as `healthy` once it has caught up.
![Exchange node in five lines](https://images.hive.blog/DQmPCCebURJ18jqqpNJ2XoBQPHe947Z1xWmzU3gRSh7NTNW/exchange-node-block-log.gif)The real run with a block log, sped up
The log stopped at the same block for minutes? > _Have you tried turning it off and on again?_ > - Roy, The IT Crowd ``` docker compose down && docker compose up -d ``` ## Your block log, three rules - Stop your old node first. - hived in the container runs as UID 1000, so it has to be able to write there: `sudo chown -R 1000 blockchain` (or your `BLOCK_LOG_DIR`). - Your block log has to be at least as new as the snapshot: it must contain the block the snapshot was made at. A node that was in sync until you stopped it is fine. An older one makes hived stop with "Chain state ... does not match block log", over and over. ## All blocks, or pruned? With a block log, the node has all blocks: either in one big file (`block-log-split = -1`) or in parts of a million blocks each (`block-log-split = 9999`, the hived default). `config.ini` says `-1`, and when the bundle finds `block_log_part.*` files it switches to `9999` for you. Want parts instead of one big file? Set `block-log-split = 9999` in `config.ini` and hived splits it on the next start. It keeps the original file, so you need the space twice until you delete it. Without a block log, the node is pruned: it runs with `block-log-split = 0` and keeps only the newest block. State is complete, and so is the account history of the accounts on the list. That is enough to follow your deposits. But `get_block` and `get_transaction` need all blocks. No block log of your own, but you want all blocks? Set this in `.env` before the first start: ``` BLOCK_LOG_URL=https://gtg.openhive.network/get/blockchain/block_log ``` The node then downloads the block log into `blockchain`, loads the snapshot, and replays only the blocks made after the snapshot. ## Is your account on the list? The snapshot has account history only for the accounts listed in `config.ini` (the `account-history-rocksdb-track-account-range` lines). On the list? You are done. Keep the list as it is. Not on the list? Then the snapshot cannot give you its history. Before the first start, add your account to `config.ini` and clear `SNAPSHOT_URL` in `.env`. With a block log the node replays all of it, with history for your account from the first block. That takes hours, not minutes. Without one, it syncs the whole chain from the P2P network, which takes even longer. Running an exchange that people actually use, and your account isn't on the list? Let me know, with a good reason, and it can be in the next snapshot. `SNAPSHOT_URL` points to `latest-1.28.8.tgz`, which is always my newest snapshot made with 1.28.8. ## The block log rule **Never download the block log twice.** Monolithic or split, keep it and reuse it for every replay and every upgrade. It is 587 GB today, and it does not get any smaller. That is what the `blockchain` folder is for. `docker compose down -v` removes the volumes, that is the state and the account history. The `blockchain` and `snapshot` folders stay. Plain `docker compose down` keeps everything. ## Bonus: asking the node The API listens on `127.0.0.1:8091` only. Keep it off the public internet. Where is the chain? ``` curl -s --data '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"database_api.get_dynamic_global_properties","id":1}' http://127.0.0.1:8091/ ``` Look for `head_block_number` and `last_irreversible_block_num`. The last 10 operations of an account. Let's take `binance-hot2`, one of Binance's accounts on the list: ``` curl -s --data '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"account_history_api.get_account_history","params":{"account":"binance-hot2","start":-1,"limit":10},"id":1}' http://127.0.0.1:8091/ ``` Each entry has the operation, its `block` and its `trx_id`. By default you get only operations from irreversible blocks, so everything you see there is final. This one works on a pruned node too. Did a transaction make it? Ask with its `trx_id`: ``` curl -s --data '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"account_history_api.get_transaction","params":{"id":"TRX_ID"},"id":1}' http://127.0.0.1:8091/ ``` If you get the transaction back, it is in an irreversible block. Until then the answer is "Unknown Transaction", and thanks to OBI that usually lasts only seconds. It needs all blocks, and it knows the transactions of the accounts on the list. And a block: ``` curl -s --data '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"block_api.get_block","params":{"block_num":BLOCK_NUM},"id":1}' http://127.0.0.1:8091/ ``` That needs all blocks too. A pruned node answers "has been pruned" for everything but the newest one. For deposits, account history is the better tool anyway: it also shows virtual operations, like recurrent transfers or transfers from savings, which you will not find in any block. It's an exchange node, but other nodes run almost the same way: a seed node, a witness node, a personal wallet node, a broadcaster, or a basic API node for your simple bots. Same compose file, a different `config.ini`, and most likely the same snapshot. hived only warns that the snapshot has more plugins than it needs. Seed and API nodes need all the blocks, though, so bring your block log.
Source: Exchange node in four lines (Hive 1.28.8) by @gtg
